findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There were a couple leaks dripping from a pipe above the right table of the dish machine. The facility is aware of the leaks and is in the process of repairing the leaks. The facility mentioned that the ice machine on the second floor is causing the leaks in the kitchen area. In the meantime, the facility is instructed to place a bucket underneath the drip to catch contaminated water. A follow-up will be scheduled for 10/8/2025 to ensure that leak is repaired and in a leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The facility was instructed to use the triple sink until the machine is functioning correctly. A follow-up is scheduled for 9/24/2025. Be sure that the dish machine is maintained at the proper concentration to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized effectively.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: There’s clean dishes stored in the dish machine that appear to be from breakfast earlier in the day. Discussed with PIC that dishes must be properly air dried and not left in the machine over night. Dishes left over night in the dish machine can be exposed to extreme moisture, possibly creating an environment where mold can grow. Ensure to place clean dishes on shelves or in a manner where they are able to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 4-901.11(A) Equipment and Utensils, Air-Drying Required. After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) Shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface SANITIZING solutions), before contact with FOOD.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: A mop was observed in the basin of the storage bucket (also storing waste water). After mopping floors, be sure to store mop heads in a manner that allows for them to properly air dry. Ensure that mop heads are never stored in dirty waste water over night. This may attract unwanted insects and pests in the kitchen area. Waste water must also be dumped at the end of the shift and never left overnight.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
There was an accumulation of pink slime on the baffles of the ice machine. PIC mentioned that the facility’s maintenance crew usually services the machine. Ensure that the ice machine baffles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent contamination. Before the cleaning process takes place, be sure to discard any ice that is currently present in the ice machine.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a couple mop heads being stored in a bucket with waste water. After each use, be sure to store mop heads in position that allows for them to properly air dry. Mops can not be stored in waste water overnight.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
